why: The student explains that int/int truncation turns the normalised row into all zeros, and fixes this failing case by casting one operand, which gives 0, 0, 0.4, 0.4, 0.2 and a row summing to 1. Locating and fixing one given failing case is L3.

concepts.why: The int claim is about division and is levelled under integer_division.
The cast is placed on the numerator before the division, so it forces real division.
Covered by the cast and normalization.

concepts.quote: All zeros, because int / int is integer division.
concepts.why: Correctly says that each count below the total of 5 truncates to 0 when the division is int.
Relates type flow to the row being a probability distribution and fixes the given case correctly.
